questions.stem: What does the word Imputation mean in the context of data?
options: Removing duplicate records
Filling in missing data
Encrypting sensitive values
Sorting data into categories
Converting text into numbers

questions.stem: In which domain is Data Imputation majorly used?
options: Data Governance
Database Administration
Network Security
Data Science
Data Archiving
questions.explanation: Data Imputation is majorly used in the Data Science domain, typically before a Machine Learning model runs.

questions.stem: Why does Data Imputation normally come into play?
options: So business rules can be imposed on all data rather than on subsets of data
So data can be stored more compactly
So sensitive values can be masked before sharing
So historical data can be retired safely
So queries can run faster on large clusters
questions.explanation: Data Imputation is used so that business rules can be applied to all of the data rather than only to the subsets that happen to be complete.

questions.stem: Before a Machine Learning model runs, which two ways of handling missing data are described for Data Imputation?
options: Encrypting the missing values or flagging them for review
Duplicating the row or moving it to an archive table
Converting the value to zero or converting it to text
Splitting the dataset or merging it with another
Filling in the missing data or removing the whole row
questions.explanation: Data imputation is done either by filling up the missing data or by removing the whole row before the model runs.

questions.stem: Which kinds of activity are said to give imperfect results when data is missing?
options: Backing up, restoring and mirroring
Compressing, archiving and indexing
Categorising, classifying and clustering
Encrypting, hashing and signing
Sorting, filtering and paging
questions.explanation: If data is missing during categorising, classifying, clustering and similar activities, the results will not be 100%.

questions.stem: In numeric datasets, what value is generally used to replace missing values?
options: The MEAN value
Zero
The maximum value
The most recent value
A randomly generated value
questions.explanation: Generally, in numeric datasets, missing values are replaced with MEAN values, although many other ways of dealing with missing data exist.

questions.stem: In the first imputation technique described, what happens to data that is missing at random?
options: It is replaced with the median of the column
It is flagged and kept in the dataset
It is estimated from a separate reference dataset
It is completely removed from the dataset before use
It is replaced with the previous row's value
questions.explanation: The first technique applies when data is missing at random and the affected data is completely removed from the dataset before it is used.

questions.stem: How does the second imputation technique treat values that are missing at random?
options: They are left blank for the model to handle
They are replaced by referring to other data points available within the current dataset
They are replaced with values from an external system
They are replaced with zero
They cause the entire dataset to be rejected
questions.explanation: In the second technique, missing values that occur at random are filled by referring to the other data points available in the current dataset.

questions.stem: The third imputation technique applies when data is NOT missing at random. How are those values mainly replaced?
options: By removing every affected column
By copying values from the nearest row
By asking the data owner to supply them
By replacing them with null markers
Using Mean, Median or Mode values
questions.explanation: When data is not missing at random, the missing values are mainly replaced using Mean, Median or Mode values.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT described as a way of dealing with missing data in Data Imputation?
options: Removing the whole row that contains the missing value
Replacing the missing value with the MEAN
Leaving the missing values in place and training the model directly on them
Replacing the value by referring to other data points in the dataset
Replacing the value with the Median or Mode
questions.explanation: Data Imputation either fills the missing values (with Mean, Median, Mode or other data points) or removes the row; leaving gaps in place for the model is not one of the described approaches.
